name: Test Execution
description: Runs EditMode tests, then PlayMode tests, and aggregates the results into a structured report. Each run_tests call returns a job_id immediately; poll each one with get_test_job and read the results from that response -- see `resultInterpretationNotes`. Tool-group activation is NOT part of the flow -- it is a conditional recovery step, kept in `conditionalRecoverySteps` below.
toolGroupNotes: `run_tests` and `get_test_job` are declared in the `testing` tool group, which the bridge reports as OFF by default -- but on the live-verified install (2026-10-21, bridge 9.6.8 over HTTP with --project-scoped-tools) every non-core tool was callable with no manage_tools call at all, and `list_groups` reported `enabled: false` for groups whose tools worked. So do NOT open this workflow with an activation step: call `run_tests` and only run the activation in `conditionalRecoverySteps` if the tool is reported as not existing. If instead the call is refused with `Tool call denied by user's permissions`, that is an IDE-side `capability: mcp` deny rule in ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml and no activation will help. `read_console` is `core`.
resultInterpretationNotes: VERIFIED on bridge 10.3.0 / Unity 6000.4.6f1, 2026-10-21, against a real EditMode test assembly with one deliberately passing and one deliberately failing test. (1) get_test_job's top-level `status` is the TEST OUTCOME, not the run's health: `succeeded` = every test that ran passed, `failed` = at least one assertion failed while the run itself was fine (the observed failing job had `error: null` and `progress.completed: 2` of `total: 2`). Do NOT debug the harness on a `failed` status -- a real harness error is a populated `error` field plus `progress.completed`/`total` that never advanced. And `succeeded` can also mean NOTHING RAN: a project with no test assemblies returned `succeeded` with `completed: 0, total: 0`. Always report the status WITH the counts. (2) Failure detail comes from `progress.failures_so_far` -- a list of {full_name, message} where `message` carries NUnit's assertion text (custom message plus Expected/But-was). It was populated in both observed runs REGARDLESS of `include_failed_tests`, and `result.results` was `null` in both; the effect of `include_failed_tests`/`include_details` on `result.results` is NOT OBSERVED, so do not set a flag expecting it to produce failure detail. (3) `result.summary` is {total, passed, failed, skipped, durationSeconds, resultState} -- observed {total:2, passed:1, failed:1, skipped:0, durationSeconds:0.33, resultState:"Failed(Child)"}. (4) Expect roughly 4 s of fixed overhead per EditMode run even for 2 trivial tests (two runs: ~4.2 s wall clock each, tests themselves 0.33 s and 0.21 s), so a few seconds of silence is not a stuck run -- watch `progress.stuck_suspected` and `progress.blocked_reason` instead. (5) `wait_timeout` (seconds) is accepted by the server with no validation error, but whether it actually blocks/long-polls is UNVERIFIED -- both observed polls happened after the job had finished. (6) PlayMode pass/fail reporting is ALSO VERIFIED on 10.3.0 (2026-10-21), against a three-test PlayMode assembly with one deliberate failure: `status: "failed"`, `mode: "PlayMode"`, `progress.completed: 3` of `total: 3`, and summary {total:3, passed:2, failed:1, skipped:0, durationSeconds:0.0716135, resultState:"Failed(Child)"} with `result.results` null. One of the two passes was a [UnityTest] coroutine asserting Time.frameCount advanced across two `yield return null`s, so frame-based PlayMode tests really execute. Points (1)-(3) above were CONFIRMED IDENTICAL in PlayMode, so read a PlayMode job exactly like an EditMode one. The MCP session survived the run's full domain reload (enterPlayModeOptionsEnabled: False), so the poll straight afterwards is safe -- but instance IDs do NOT survive it, which is a separate rule and unchanged. Measured wall clock ~5.2 s vs EditMode's ~4.2 s. (7) STILL UNVERIFIED: whether a smaller `init_timeout` suffices for PlayMode (120000 was passed on the verified run -- keep it), the test_names/group_names/category_names filters, and clear_stuck. The `assembly_names` filter IS verified in both modes. `manage_build`, used to pair test runs with per-platform builds, is also UNVERIFIED -- a `capability: mcp` / `effect: deny` rule in the user's own ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml blocked every attempt, which is the user's security decision, not a defect in this Power or the bridge; report the matched rule and stop.

conditionalRecoverySteps.name: CONDITIONAL -- run only if run_tests/get_test_job is reported as not existing: activate the `testing` tool group, then re-try. The MCP client may need a refresh or reconnect before a newly activated tool appears.

steps.name: Start EditMode tests (returns job_id; poll separately with get_test_job -- EditMode pass/fail reporting is VERIFIED on 10.3.0)

Start PlayMode tests (returns job_id; poll separately with get_test_job -- PlayMode pass/fail reporting is VERIFIED on 10.3.0, and the response shape is identical to EditMode's). It starts with a domain reload, so keep init_timeout 120000 as upstream recommends -- the verified run passed it, and whether a smaller value suffices is UNVERIFIED. A PlayMode test assembly needs includePlatforms: [] in its .asmdef, not ["Editor"].
Aggregate test results -- the authoritative source is each job's get_test_job response (result.summary plus progress.failures_so_far); this console read is supplementary context only
